name: MOZAMBIQUE

flag.title: Flag of Mozambique
flag.note: AK-47 on a flag — unique in the world

lead: Mozambique stretches along south-east Africa where savanna, wetland, and golden beach meet the warm Indian Ocean. Portuguese traders arrived 500 years ago; today the country blends African, Arab, and Portuguese flavours — piri-piri prawns, Makonde carvings, and marrabenta music drifting from a seaside café.

geo: Mozambique's Indian Ocean coastline runs 2,470 km — one of Africa's longest — laced with coral reefs, mangroves, and islands like the palm-fringed Bazaruto Archipelago. Great rivers including the Zambezi cross the country and fan into vast deltas before reaching the sea.

Inland, flat coastal plains rise to highland plateaus and the Chimanimani Mountains, where Monte Binga reaches 2,436 m on the Zimbabwe border. The wide interior is a mosaic of miombo woodland and wetlands that flood gloriously every rainy season.
animals: The Bazaruto Archipelago shelters East Africa's last healthy dugong colony — gentle sea-cow relatives grazing on seagrass in turquoise bays. Whale sharks and manta rays cruise the same waters October to April, and five turtle species nest on the beaches.

Inland, Gorongosa National Park bounced back from near-total collapse; a 2024 survey counted 110,000 large animals including lions, elephants, and hippos. Over 750 bird species live here — more than all of mainland Europe.
culture: Mozambican cooking is a happy mash-up: piri-piri chilli fires up prawns and grilled chicken; cassava and coconut-milk stews reflect Bantu roots; Arabic flatbreads appear in the north. Piri-piri sauce, arguably the country's greatest food export, is now eaten worldwide.

Music is everywhere. Marrabenta — born on homemade guitars built from oil cans and fishing wire in the 1950s — has a bouncy beat perfect for dancing. The Chopi people are famed for their timbila xylophone orchestras, which UNESCO recognised as a masterpiece of oral heritage.
history: Arab traders reached Mozambique's coast around 800 CE, building wealthy Swahili city-states. Vasco da Gama anchored here in 1498, and the country became a key stop on Portugal's spice route to India, ruled from the tiny Island of Mozambique — a UNESCO World Heritage site.

A ten-year independence war ended in 1975 when FRELIMO won freedom. A brutal sixteen-year civil war followed, killing over a million people. Peace arrived in 1992, and Mozambique rebuilt — Gorongosa is now Africa's greatest wildlife comeback story.
wows: Mozambique is the only country whose name contains all five vowels: A, E, I, O, U.
Its flag is the only national flag on Earth to show an AK-47 assault rifle.
A Portuguese chapel built here in 1522 is the oldest European building in the southern hemisphere.
Mozambique has 750+ bird species — about 50 more than all of continental Europe.
Bazaruto holds Africa's last viable east-coast dugong colony: ~250–350 animals.
In Scrabble, 'Mozambique' scores 34 points — the highest of any one-word country.
Gorongosa's 2024 survey found 110,000 large animals, up from near-zero after civil war.

myths.fact: Most of Mozambique is lush tropical savanna with great rivers, wetlands, and coral reefs. The Sahara Desert is thousands of kilometres to the north.
Popular areas — Maputo, Inhambane, Bazaruto — are well-established destinations with good infrastructure, visited safely by thousands each year.
